description:
FILED s450u (Opus, round 8 agent U), found by a design probe while shipping
#477.  PRE-EXISTING (nothing in s450u touches $. â the probe was asked
because the p-magic-cell mechanism was a CANDIDATE representation for
$&/$`/$', and this is why it was not used).

A magic scalar that is represented as a p-box holding a p-magic-cell (getter
+ setter, intercepted at unbox/box-set) is a SHARED CONTAINER, so every use
site that stores the variable stores the same box â and every reader then
sees the CURRENT value, not the value at the time of the store.  `$.` is the
one such variable today (`(defvar |$.| (make-p-box (make-p-magic-cell â¦)))`).

    open my $fh, '<', $0 or die;
    my @lines;
    while (my $l = <$fh>) { push @lines, $.; last if $. >= 3; }
    close $fh;
    print "pushed: @lines\n";
    my $a = $.; my $b = $.;
    print "copies: $a $b\n";

    perl 5.40.3:   pushed: 1 2 3      PCL:  pushed: 3 3 3     <-- silent wrong
                   copies: 0 0              copies: 3 3       <-- second bug

TWO bugs in four lines:

(a) THE ALIAS.  `push @lines, $.` must push the VALUE.  Every place that
    copies a box into a container has to read a magic cell through its getter
    first â the same rule `unbox`/`box-sv`/`box-nv` already follow at their
    own chokepoints.  Find the container-store path (p-push and the list
    flattener) and make a magic-cell box arrive as its value; the assignment
    `my $a = $.` has the same shape and the same fix.

(b) `$.` after an explicit `close` is 0 in perl (perlvar: close resets the
    line counter for that handle), 3 in PCL.  `%p-dot-get` reads
    `*p-last-read-handle*`'s entry in `*p-fh-lines*`; p-close does not clear
    it.

Neither is behind a counted row today (found by probe, not by a failing
test).  (a) is the serious one: it is a SILENT WRONG of exactly the #138
family's kind â a plausible-looking answer.  Do (a) first and probe (b) in
the same session, since the fix touches the same variable.


=== HALF (a) DONE (s473v, 2026-09-16) ===
`push @lines, $.` now records each line number: perl `1 2 3`, PCL `1 2 3`
(the base tree gives `3 3 3`).  The fix is ONE arm in %p-array-store-scalar
-- an array store of a box holding a MAGIC CELL stores the cell`s VALUE --
and it was needed by #1804, which made / elements magic cells the way
perl`s are and would otherwise have made `my @c = @-` follow the next
match.  Guard: Pl/t/match-vars-01.t row 50 (inverse-verified: it FAILS on a
2ac855aa extraction).

HALF (b) IS STILL OPEN: `$.` after `close` is 0 in perl and 3 in PCL
(re-probed s473v, scratch/s473v/probe/dot683b.pl) -- that is the per-handle
counter`s reset rule, a different question from the container one.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a p-magic-cell box is a SHARED CONTAINER, so `push @lines, $.` pushes the box -- perl 1 2 3, PCL 3 3 3 (and $. is not reset by close)
